cards.name: BrshIdx

Read as data it is an index of 216 brush entries keyed by Corel default IDs (e.g. '1:CorelDefaultID_500:CorelDefaultID_504'), in two groups of 139 and 77, so it most likely stores the brush picker's list and order. No thumbnail: the renderer found no zlib preview in the .pst (render failed), so nothing about a look is verified.
use_for: keeping a user's brush list when migrating or backing up the CorelDRAW user profile (copy the whole Presets/Brush folder)
avoid: Looking for a stroke style here: the look is unverified (render failed) and the file is an index of brush IDs, not a brush; pick a named brush preset instead (e.g. the Content/Painter/Brushes presets).
Editing or deleting it by hand: the format is undocumented; back up the folder first.
cards.applies_to: none directly: a brush-list support file that CorelDRAW reads from the user profile (which brush tool owns it was not harvested); it is not applied to an object
cards.how_to_apply: Nothing to apply: no menu, docker or call loads it by name, and the harvest records only the file: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite 2024\Custom Data\Presets\Brush\BrshIdx.pst. CorelDRAW reads it itself from the user's Custom Data/Presets/Brush folder.

verified.note: No thumbnail (render failed: no zlib preview in the .pst); reading the file confirms 216 '<n>:CorelDefaultID_...' entries in two groups of 139 ('1:') and 77 ('4:').

cards.name: BrshImg

Read as data it holds 202 zlib-compressed 24-bit bitmaps, each a small wide strip (about 160-194 px wide, 4-42 px tall) showing a grey or black brush-stroke sample: solid and tapered lines, soft airbrush bands, speckled spray, multi-bristle and dotted strokes, i.e. the brush picker's stroke previews. The sheet render failed (zlib 'invalid stored block lengths'), so there is no gallery thumbnail.

avoid: Looking for a stroke style here: the file is a store of about 200 small preview strips, not one brush; pick a named brush preset instead (e.g. the Content/Painter/Brushes presets).
Copying it without BrshIdx.pst: the two files presumably belong together (not tested); keep the folder whole.

cards.name: Aztec
cards.summary: Bump-map image shipped in CorelDRAW 2024's Custom Data/Bumpmap folder, the height map that Effects > Custom > Bump Map lights as relief (bright = high, dark = low). The thumbnail is the file itself (file image, not a script render): white rectangles of mixed sizes fitted together and separated by thick, soft-edged dark grey grooves, like interlocking stone slabs or Aztec stonework. As a bump map the slabs come out raised and the grooves sunken.
use_for: paving or stone-wall relief on a background photo
Aztec / temple stonework look for game or adventure posters
chunky block relief behind a headline
avoid: Expecting it to change an object by itself: it is only the height map for Effects > Custom > Bump Map (or an image you import); it does nothing to a selected object on its own.

Scripted runs: the map image has no command value in Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect('BumpMapEffect ...'), so a script gets whatever map the dialog last held; choose the map in the dialog, or use Effects/3D Effects/Emboss for relief built from the image itself.
Colour: the map is grayscale; colour comes from the bitmap underneath and the effect's light colours.
cards.applies_to: bitmap: the map image is chosen inside the Bump Map effect, which works on a bitmap object (convert vectors first with Object > Convert to Bitmap); the file itself is a grayscale height map, not applied to an object directly
cards.how_to_apply: Select a bitmap, Effects > Custom > Bump Map, on the Bump Map page pick the map named after this file ('Aztec'; the dialog's map list was not harvested, this folder is where the shipped maps live), set Scaling Mode (Tile or Stretch To Fit), Scale Factor and the lights, then OK. Menu by script: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("e7564762-4f00-4dc2-9ddc-aac4809fc5f7") opens the dialog (modal, a person presses OK). Unattended: s.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("Bump Map", "BumpMapEffect ScalingMode=Tile,ScaleFactor=100") runs with the map the dialog last held (the map has no command value). The file can also be imported as a bitmap: ActiveLayer.Import("C:\Program Files\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite\25\Custom Data\Bumpmap\Aztec.cpt").

verified.note: White rectangles of mixed sizes fitted together and separated by thick, soft-edged near-black grooves.
